description.value: The study examined relationships among gray-matter volume, dopamine D2/D3 receptor availability, and methamphetamine craving in methamphetamine users and control participants.

spans.text: The goal of the current study was to examine the relationships between dopamine D2/D3 receptor availability (binding potential relative to nondisplaceable uptake of the radiotracer; BP ) using positron emission tomography (PET), gray-matter volume measured using high-resolution structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and self-reported craving for methamphetamine.

description.value: Observational comparison of methamphetamine users and healthy controls, with MRI and PET scanning during abstinence.

spans.text: Ninety-five participants (58 methamphetamine users, 37 healthy controls) were included in this study.

value: In methamphetamine users, midbrain D2/D3 BP was positively associated with gray-matter volume in bilateral striatum, amygdala, hippocampus, temporal pole, inferior frontal gyrus, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, and insula, while no significant associations were detected in controls.

The positive relationship between midbrain D2/D3 BP and gray-matter volume in the methamphetamine group but not in the control group suggests that capacity for regulating dopamine signaling may influence methamphetamine-induced neurotoxicity in brain regions that receive dopaminergic projections from the midbrain.

spans.text: In the methamphetamine group, midbrain D2/D3 BP  was positively associated with gray-matter volume in bilateral striatum, amygdala, hippocampus, temporal pole, inferior frontal gyrus, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, and insula ( Figure 2B ,  Supplemental Table 1 ), while no significant associations between gray-matter volume and midbrain D2/D3 BP  were detected in the control group (p’s > 0.4; see  Supplemental Figures 2 and 3  for scatter plots and effect size maps).

value: Group-by-striatal D2/D3 BP interactions were detected on gray-matter volume of bilateral striatum, left pallidum, and temporal cortex, reflecting positive correlations between striatal D2/D3 BP and gray-matter volume in the methamphetamine group but no significant correlations in the control group.

These associations remained significant in the methamphetamine group after including midbrain D2/D3 BP as a covariate, suggesting that additional factors that influence the extent of neurotoxicity or that predate drug use influence the association between striatal BP and gray-matter volume in methamphetamine users.

A magnetization-prepared rapid acquisition gradient echo sequence

A magnetization-prepared rapid acquisition gradient echo sequence (TR=1900 ms, TE=4.38 ms, flip angle=15°, FOV=256×256×160, 160 slices, thickness: 1-mm) was run on a 1.5- Tesla Siemens Sonata scanner (Erlangen, Germany) with a standard quadrature head coil to produce high-resolution, T1-weighted, MRIs.
